clue.text: Beethoven's fifth penguin?

definitions.meaning: Beethoven's Fifth Piano Concerto carries the nickname by which it is widely known
the largest species of penguin, with the question mark flagging a definition by example

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a symphony and a seabird, as if the music had become an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's fifth' tempts toward the Fifth Symphony or the letter V; it is the Fifth Piano Concerto, nicknamed for a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are names: the concerto's nickname, and the Antarctic species, the largest living penguin.

clue.text: Two cases of executives catching better flights

indicators.note: catching means trapping, so one piece is held inside the other
two says the selected pair of letters appears twice
cases of means the outer letters, the case around the word executives

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: Executives with two briefcases get better flights.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of executives give ES; doubled, ESES, with CAP caught in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Getaways or escapes from captivity are flights, as in the flight of refugees.

clue.text: Gradually admit ropy Spanish hasn't succeeded when touring Spain

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the anagram goes round the Spain letter
ropy means poor or shoddy, so these letters are arranged badly
hasn't says one letter is not present in the word Spanish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone's poor Spanish is not getting by while travelling round Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't' removes an S from SPANISH; 'ropy' reorders the rest as PHASIN, which goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce something in stages is to admit it gradually, a phrasal verb.

clue.text: Give another brief brush to ancient artefact?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again, making another of something

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter of the word for brush goes

parts.note: a lick of paint is a quick brush

explanation.surface: Someone gives an old artefact another quick dusting.
explanation.walkthrough: RE plus LICK, cut short by 'brief' to LIC; 'Give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A surviving object from the distant past is an ancient artefact; the question mark admits it may be another thing.

clue.text: Barking terrier, extremely virile dog

indicators.note: barking means mad, so these letters are crazily rearranged
extremely means at the extremes, the outer letters of virile

explanation.surface: A terrier is barking at a very virile dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like a dog noise but is the anagram signal for TERRIER plus VE.
explanation.definitionFit: The gun-dog breed bred to fetch shot game is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Pompous knights finally unseated in joust

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word knights

parts.note: tilted means toppled over, as a rider knocked down in a tilt or joust

explanation.surface: Arrogant knights are finally knocked off their horses in a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff, unnatural and overformal speech or manner is pompous; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Orgy superseded on a regular basis

indicators.note: on a regular basis means taking every other letter of superseded

explanation.surface: A wild party is regularly replaced by another.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of wild unrestrained indulgence is an orgy, as in a spending or drinking binge.

clue.text: He tips off six-footer currently playing well, perhaps

parts.note: a player on top of their game is said to be in form
an ant, like any insect, has six feet

explanation.surface: A tall footballer who is on good form passes on a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is an insect. The wordplay reads as the ant being in form.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who passes secret information to the police is a person who tips them off.

clue.text: Puny competitor, one entering after start of tournament

indicators.note: after places the competitor piece behind the opening letter
start of points to the opening letter of tournament
entering means going inside, so one goes into the competitor

parts.note: a rival is a competitor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A feeble competitor enters after the tournament has started.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trifling or of slight importance is puny; both mean insignificant.

clue.text: Stubborn folk slip into islands

parts.note: to don a garment is to slip into it
keys are low islands or reefs, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: Obstinate people sneak into some islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses are proverbially obstinate, so stubborn people are called by the animal's name.

clue.text: Silent movie star's sacrificed in film — wreath produced

indicators.note: sacrificed says the star's name gives up the word in, which is dropped from it

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin was the great star of silent cinema
taken as written
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A silent film star's career is lost in a movie, and a wreath is laid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacrificed' drops the word 'in' from the star's surname; 'in' looks like a link word but is the piece removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland or circlet of flowers worn on the head is a wreath, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Went on securing gallery, ejecting one unknown thug

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast inside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: went on, as in continued, means ran

indicators.note: ejecting says letters are thrown out of the gallery's name

parts.note: the Uffizi is the famous art gallery in Florence
one is I, the Roman numeral
an unknown in algebra is often Z

explanation.surface: A thug kept going after breaking into an art gallery, having thrown someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejecting' removes I and Z from UFFIZI, leaving UFFI, which RAN holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent, lawless person is a thug; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Writer tails academic, ignoring university order

indicators.note: tails means follows behind, so the writer comes second
ignoring means leaving out the abbreviation for university

parts.note: academic, as in pure science rather than applied, means pure
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A journalist follows a professor around, ignoring the university's instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' takes U out of PURE, leaving PRE; SCRIBE tails it.
explanation.definitionFit: To order a remedy or course of action, as a doctor does, is to direct it: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Eau de Cologne?

parts.note: read literally in French, the water of Cologne: the river flowing through that German city

explanation.walkthrough: The perfume is a decoy: 'eau' is simply water, and Cologne's water is its river.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river that runs through Cologne is literally that city's water, as the French words say.

clue.text: Convention — Whitby's last hosted by retiring fellows?

indicators.note: hosted by means taken in as a guest, so one piece sits inside the other
retiring means going backwards, so the word for fellows is read right to left

parts.note: fellows of a college are dons

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of Whitby

explanation.surface: A gathering in Whitby is hosted by college fellows who are going into retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns DONS into SNOD; Y, the end of Whitby, goes inside. The Synod of Whitby (664) was a famous church council.
explanation.definitionFit: A church council or assembly is a convention of clergy, a formal meeting.

clue.text: Import deal possibly giving source of free fuel?

parts.note: the import of a speech is its gist, its drift
deal is pine or fir timber, an example of wood

explanation.surface: A trade import might provide fuel at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Import' and 'deal' look like trade words; one means meaning, the other a timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber washed ashore can be gathered for nothing and burned, hence a free supply of fuel.

clue.text: Arabs live all over the place — their values may change

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arabs live scattered widely, and their values may shift.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as cultural comment; in mathematics, quantities whose values may change are this.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra and programming, symbols standing for quantities that can take different values are named for that changeability.

clue.text: Left-winger skirting last carriage run over

indicators.note: skirting means going around the edges, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
a hearse is the vehicle for a final journey

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician avoids a funeral car and is run over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run over' looks like a traffic accident; here it means practised.
explanation.definitionFit: To run over a play or speech is to go through it in practice; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Old man's tract of land through which inlet runs

indicators.note: through which says something passes through the middle of the land piece

parts.note: a patch is a small plot or tract of land
a ria is a long narrow sea inlet formed by a drowned river valley
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An elderly man owns a plot of land with a creek running through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through which' sends both the inlet and the runs abbreviation into the middle of the land piece; a ria is a drowned river valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A family head or venerable elder is an old man of authority; the word means a male elder.

clue.text: There's talk of someone preserving a book of holy songs

indicators.note: talk of says the word is spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a salter preserves meat or fish with salt

explanation.surface: People say someone is keeping a hymn book.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume of the Psalms for worship is a book of sacred songs.

clue.text: Skilled amateur in union creating scene

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: TU stands for trade union
able means skilled or competent

explanation.surface: A skilled amateur in a trade union stages a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A posed group or striking picture, as in a tableau vivant, is a scene.

clue.text: British unit essential to further measurement

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A British unit is vital to taking further measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heat once used for British gas bills, equal to 100,000 British thermal units.

clue.text: Priest on team heartily curses exotic preparations

parts.note: Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Bible
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

indicators.note: heartily means taking the heart, the middle letters of curses

explanation.surface: A priest swears heartily at his team over strange potions.
explanation.definitionFit: Magical potions or remedies, like alchemists' elixirs of life, are exotic preparations.

clue.text: Old Amerindian's lost a sheep going up country

indicators.note: lost says a letter is dropped from the Amerindian word

parts.note: the Maya were an ancient people of Central America

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An ancient American has lost a sheep wandering up the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' drops one A from MAYAN, leaving MYAN; RAM 'going up' gives MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southeast Asian nation formerly known as Burma is a country.

clue.text: Reach maiden in topless dress

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
topless means losing the top, the first letter of the word for dress

parts.note: a habit is a garment, as worn by a nun or rider
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl reaches for a dress with no top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts H from HABIT, leaving ABIT, and M goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope or extent, how far something extends, is its reach: a noun synonym.

clue.text: Liar hangs out in idyllic location

indicators.note: out means not as normal, or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A liar hangs about in a beautiful place.
explanation.definitionFit: The hidden Himalayan valley paradise of James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, now any earthly paradise.

clue.text: Firm dealt in clothing items, primarily

indicators.note: clothing means dressing around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a trader who dealt in goods sold them

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of items

explanation.surface: A firm traded in clothing articles above all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm is solid, steady and not liable to give way: adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Superficial damage to crop

definitions.meaning: a slight scrape or abrasion of the skin
to crop is to eat grass, as cattle do in a field

explanation.surface: Light harm is done to a harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape on the skin is superficial damage, and animals feeding on grass crop it.

clue.text: Whistle-blower stops hard labour in plant

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so one piece fills the middle of the other

parts.note: toil is hard labour
a referee, the ref, blows the whistle in a match

explanation.surface: An informer puts an end to hard labour in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informer; here it is a referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover and similar three-leaved herbs belong to this group, so it names a kind of plant.

clue.text: One type of publicity I must spread round arena

indicators.note: spread round means scattered about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is one form of publicity

explanation.surface: An advertiser insists on putting posters all round a sports venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread round' is the anagram signal; 'One type of publicity' gives an abbreviation before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sports ground with banked seating is an arena, a venue for contests.

clue.text: Mature sycophantic journalists might gather here

definitions.meaning: fully developed, as a full-bodied wine or a well-developed character

explanation.surface: A seasoned person notices where fawning reporters would congregate.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as ROUND ED: ED is the usual short form of editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-developed, fully formed character or wine is called mature.

clue.text: Storage cabinet provided by bald barber?

indicators.note: bald means without hair, so that word is removed

parts.note: a barber cuts hair for a living, a hairdresser

explanation.surface: A bald barber has supplied a cupboard for a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: A barber is a HAIRDRESSER; 'bald' strips off HAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen sideboard with shelves for dishes is a cabinet for storage.
